receipt: Atlas can now represent and materialize reproducible code-change candidates behind an explicit isolated-tree-write capability boundary. A zero-spend probe produced two distinct alternatives for the same atomic-ingestion repair hypothesis from one exact base, preserved per-file before/after digests and rollback data, rejected base drift, and left the source tree unchanged while experimenting. This closes the first materialization step for handing D an executable candidate without hiding shell commands or choosing a winner.
